title: Sharing what has become clear
meaning: You can share personal understanding calmly and deeply when a considered conclusion remains an invitation to answer rather than a settled truth for both of you.
text: The Hermit’s three roles on your Vishuddha do not simply mean shared silence. In the physical position, he appears in voicing a considered conclusion and sharing its grounds. In energy, he supports the wish for substantial understanding: finding what genuinely lies behind the words. In emotions, he brings a quiet sense of inward clarity. Conversation may have an unhurried rhythm, but its purpose is to make personal understanding available to each other.

For example, you return to the ordinary question “How was your day?” and explain why an immediate answer can sometimes be difficult. Reflection reveals that before recounting events, you want to understand which of them mattered. **Personal clarity becomes shared through telling its story**. You can offer one meaning you have found rather than listing everything. A different detail appears in reply, and the conversation gains depth without requiring lengthy speech or turning the evening into a compulsory review of experience.

Difficulty arises if personal clarity starts to seem like a sufficient explanation for you both. The other person’s question may then sound like interference with a settled conclusion, while calm becomes closed finality. The constructive wish to understand more deeply helps you hear the different experience an answer reveals. A considered thought retains its value when it can be shared, clarified and enriched without defending it against every new question.
